conversation.contentPreview:
Build a Todo app in a single self-contained HTML file. Requirements:
- Add new todos
- Mark todos as complete (strikethrough)
- Delete todos
- Filter: All / Active / Completed
- Persist to localStorage

Deliver only the HTML file with JS, CSS, HTML. Use file name "todo_anthropic-claude-sonnet-5_01.html"

toolCallDetails.arguments:
{"path":"todo_anthropic-claude-sonnet-5_01.html","edit_description":"Create a complete, self-contained single-file Todo app (HTML+CSS+JS all in one file, no external dependencies).

Requirements:
- Clean modern UI with a centered card layout, gradient background, nice typography, rounded corners, subtle shadows.
- Header with title "Todo" and a subtitle.
- Input form at top: text input with placeholder "What needs to be done?" plus an "Add" button. Pressing Enter also adds the todo. Ignore empty/whitespace-only input.
- Each todo item shows: a checkbox (custom styled) to toggle complete, the todo text (with CSS text-decoration line-through and reduced opacity when completed), and a delete button (e.g. an "×" icon button) that removes it with a small fade/slide-out animation.
- Filter bar with three buttons: "All", "Active", "Completed" — clicking sets active filter (visually highlighted with an active class) and re-renders the filtered list without losing the other todos.
- Footer/status bar showing count of remaining active (not completed) items, e.g. "3 items left", and a "Clear completed" button that removes all completed todos (only enabled/shown when there are completed items).
- Empty state message shown when there are no todos matching the current filter (e.g. "No todos yet" / "No active todos" / "No completed todos").
- Persistence: store the todos array (each with id, text, completed) as JSON in localStorage under a key like "todos-app-v1"; load from localStorage on page load; save to localStorage after every add/toggle/delete/clear-completed action.
- All JavaScript must be vanilla JS (no frameworks/CDN libraries), inline in a <script> tag. All CSS inline in a <style> tag in <head>. Everything in this ONE html file, fully self-contained, works when opened directly via file:// in a browser.
- Use semantic HTML, reasonable accessibility (labels/aria where sensible), and responsive layout that looks good on mobile widths too.
- Add a small HTML comment at the top noting it's a self-contained single-file todo app."}
